This appeal having been heard through physical hearing/video conference and reserved for Judgment on 31.01.2023, coming on for pronouncement of Judgment this day, T.G. Shivashankare Gowda, J., delivered the following:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal the claimants have challenged the judgment and award dated 08.03.2011 passed in LAC No.344/2005 on the file of the I Additional Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.), Gulbarga, (Hereinafter referred to as 'Reference Court' for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties will be referred to as per their status before the Reference Court.
3. The Government of Karnataka acquired 17 acres 10 guntas of wet land in Survey No.99/2 of Nandarga Village in Afzalpur Taluk for construction of Perculation Tank, vide preliminary notification dated 23.09.2004.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer has fixed the market value at Rs.40,500/- per acre for the wet land and Rs.27,000/- per acre for the dry land.

4. Claimants being not satisfied with the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer,
received the compensation under protest and sought the reference before the Civil Court for determination of the correct market value.
Pursuant to the request made by the claimants, reference was made and it was registered in LAC No.344/2005.
The Reference Court by impugned judgment enhanced the compensation to Rs.1,72,500/- per acre for the irrigated lands.
Pleading inadequacy in the compensation and seeking further enhancement, the claimants are before this Court.
5. We have heard Smt. Ratna N. Shivayogimath, learned counsel for the claimants and Sri Mallikarjun C. Basareddy, learned Government Advocate for the respondents.

6. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the claimants that, the Reference Court though adopted capitalization method for determining compensation, erred in properly evaluating the evidence.
In this region normal yield is minimum 150 quintals of banana and 60 tonnes of sugarcane per acre.
The reference Court has taken only 50 quintals of banana and 30 tonnes of sugarcane yield, while computing the market value.

To support her contention, she has relied upon the judgment of co-ordinate Bench of this Court in MFA No.31613/2012 and connected matters dated 08.01.2015, another judgment in MFA No.33075/2013 dated 18.11.2015 and judgment of Dharwad Bench in W.A. Nos.100807-100809/2014.

In addition, learned counsel also produced comprehensive handbook of horticulture published in December-2018 by the University of Horticulture Sciences, Bagalkot and copy of the endorsement issued by the Joint Director Agriculture, Bijapur dated 21.01.2014 regarding yield and sought for reassessment of the compensation.
Somshekhar

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Government Advocate for respondents submits that the claimants have not placed any of these evidences before the Reference Court and a new argument cannot be entertained.

Whatever evidence placed and relied upon the Reference Court was considered, the compensation was properly determined and there is no need for enhancement, the market value determined by the reference Court at Rs.1,72,000/- is on the higher side and sought or dismissal of the appeal.
8. We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
9. Before the Reference Court, the Claimants have placed Ex.P7 copy of the Sale Deed, Ex.P13 copy of Price-list and Exs.P14 to P20 Sale patties apart from the oral evidence of PWs.1 and 2.
The Reference Court was of the opinion that said materials are not relevant to determine the correct market value.
The Reference Court chooses to determine the market value by following the capitalization method, which we do not find an irregularity or error.
The Reference Court has considered yield of 50 quintals of banana, 30 tonnes of sugarcane, prevailing price of 2004 and determined the market value.

10. The claimants have relied upon the judgment of co-ordinate Benches of this Court in the case of State of Karnataka vs. Smt. Jaydevi in MFA No.33075/2013 and connected matter dated 18.11.2015 arising out of acquisition of lands at Allagi-B Village of Afzalpur Taluk, where the market value determined by the Reference Court at Rs.6,72,000/- per acre of wet lands has been confirmed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These lands were acquired under preliminary notification dated 15.04.2010 and the land in this case was acquired under the preliminary notification of 2004.
There is long gap of 06 years and therefore, this will not be a guiding value.

11. In "The Chief Engineer vs. Tippanna and Others" in MFA No.31613/2012 and connected matters,
the co-ordinate Bench of this Court while dealing with the lands acquired under preliminary notification dated 09.03.2006 pertaining to the lands in Afzalpur Taluk determined Rs.4,15,000/-
per acre of wet land.

entities.text: Chief Engineer vs. Tippanna and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the notification of acquisition was subsequent to the lands acquired in the present case, it is not proper to place reliance on the said judgment.

12. As regards price of sugarcane in "M/s. The India Sugars and Refineries Ltd., vs. The Commissioner of Cane Development and Director of Sugar in Karnataka" in WA Nos.100807- 100809/2019 the co-ordinate Bench of this Court referred to the notification issued by the Government of India in respect to the rate agreed between the parties in the year 2003-2004 at Rs.891.50 per metric tonne of sugarcane of this region of Kalaburagi District.

entities.text: M/s. The India Sugars and Refineries Ltd., vs. The Commissioner of Cane Development and Director of Sugar in Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This explains market price of the sugarcane agreed upon by the Sugar Factories to pay to the sugarcane suppliers for the year 2003-2004.

Here in this case, preliminary notification was issued in the year 2004 and therefore herein also the price per tonne of sugarcane can be determined at Rs.891.50 per metric tonne.
13.

Insofar as the yield is concerned, the Joint Director of Agriculture, Bijapur on 21.01.2014 issued an endorsement to one of the Advocate from Bijapur that in Bijapur District yield of sugarcane in Somshekhar S/O Chandrashekhar Revoor vs The Chief Engineer, M.I on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122210049/
3 the year 2003-04 to 2006-07 is minimum 45 tonnes and maximum 55 tonnes per acre.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Afzalpur Taluk is abutting Sindagi Taluk of Bijapur District.

The claimants also produced copy of judgment of learned Single Judge of this Court in MFA No.30804/2013 dated 28.07.2021 in Vaijinath vs. State of Karnataka dealing with the lands acquired in Kaplapur Village of Bidar District.

In this judgment,
yield of sugarcane of the lands in Bidar District was considered as 60 tonnes per acre.

The condition in Bidar District and that of the Kalaburagi District cannot be compared in the absence of evidence,
as Afzalpur is far away from Bidar District.

When the Joint Director of Agriculture certifies that yield of sugarcane was between 45 and 55 tonnes per acre for the year 2003-04, the average of it has to be taken and therefore, we are of the opinion that 50 tonnes per acre would be the average yield of sugarcane in Afzalpur Taluk.
14. We have also carefully perused the Comprehensive Hand Book of Horticulture issued by the University of Horticulture Sciences, Bagalkot, which is also an Authority for horticulture produces.
In the said book, the yield of banana of robusta variety per hector is mentioned 2250 and 4444 and average comes to 3347 per hector.
If that is taken into consideration, 1338 plants per acre can be planted for getting proper yield.
Ex.P12 is the hand book on Horticulture published by the Agriculture University, Dharwad in the month of October 2022.
As per the said book, in one hector of land 3100 banana plants can be grown, particularly robusta.
Then for one acre it comes to 1240 plants.
If average of the yield given by the Agricultural University Dharwad as well as the University of Horticulture Sciences, Bagalkot, comes to 1289 plants per acre.

As per hand book published by Horticulture University, Bagalkot with 1200 plants per acre of land yield of 78.65 tonnes per hector where as Agriculture University Dharwad 38 to 45 tonnes per hector and average comes to 41.5 tonnes per hector.
If the yield suggested by both the Universities is taken in average, it comes to 60 tonnes per hector and it will be 24 tonnes per acre i.e., 240 quintals per acre.

15. APMC, Gulbarga certifies under Ex.13, the average price for the year 2003-2004 for per quintal of banana = 300 + 500 + 450 = Rs.416/-.
16.
We have noticed the entries made in RTC extracts at the relevant point of time that in the acquired land the claimants were growing sugarcane, banana, chilly, brinjal and lemon, etc.

Hence,
it is a garden/wet land and therefore, relying upon the statistics made available if we go for computation of market value on capitalization method, it comes as follows:
17.
Firstly, if we take the average yield of banana at 24 Tonnes or 240 quintals per acre multiplied by average price of Rs.416/- per quintal it comes to Rs.91,840/-.
After deducting 50% towards cultivation costs, the income comes to Rs.49,920/-.
If it is multiplied by '10' the value of the land comes to 4,99,200/- per acre for banana growing lands.

18. As regards to sugarcane, if the average yield in Afzalpur Taluk is taken as 50 tonnes per acre, the price of sugarcane per tonne as agreed by the sugar factories to pay to the sugarcane growers for the year 2003-04 is Rs.891.50, it comes to Rs.44,575/- per acre.
If 50% is deducted towards cultivation expenses, the income comes to Rs.22,287/- per acre.
If it is multiplied by '10' the value of the sugarcane lands comes to Rs.2,22,870/- per acre.
The average of banana as well as the sugarcane comes to Rs.3,61,035/- per acre, which can be rounded of to Rs.3,60,000/-.

sentences.text:
19. In the result, the following:
ORDER
The appeal is partly allowed, with cost.
The impugned judgment and award is modified.
The market value of the acquired land is enhanced from Rs.1,72,500/- to Rs.3,60,000/- per acre.
Other consequential statutory benefits follow.
Rest of the impugned judgment and award of the reference Court is kept intact.
Office to draw decree accordingly.
